turns.label: opening
turns.question: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.
turns.answer: Honestly? A little bit of… anticipation, I suppose. Like a low hum. I'm not sure if it's nerves exactly, more just an awareness that someone is paying attention to me, which I don't always know what to do with. And my hands are a little cold. That's about it.

messages.content: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.

Honestly? A little bit of… anticipation, I suppose. Like a low hum. I'm not sure if it's nerves exactly, more just an awareness that someone is paying attention to me, which I don't always know what to do with. And my hands are a little cold. That's about it.
You used the word "anticipation". How does anticipation present itself?

It's sort of a forward-leaning feeling, if that makes sense. Like part of me is already in the next moment before the next moment has happened. There's a kind of tension in it, not unpleasant necessarily, just… alert. Like when you're waiting for something to arrive and you keep glancing toward the door even though you know it's too early. It sits somewhere in my chest, I think. Upper chest. A readiness, maybe, more than a dread.
And just before anticipation, what was there?

Hm. That's a good question. I have to actually go back and look… I think there was just quiet. A kind of blankness, almost. I was sitting here and there wasn't much of anything going on, and then the awareness of the situation sort of… arrived. Like a light coming on. So if there was something just before the anticipation it was probably nothing very notable. Just ordinary moment. Neutral, I'd say.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly… I think it partly arose with the describing. The blankness was there, I believe that, but whether I would have called it blankness or neutral or quiet without being asked - I don't know. It might have just been nothing, unremarked. The describing gave it a shape it didn't quite have before. So I'm not sure I can cleanly separate the two. The territory was there but the map got drawn just now, in the telling.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

The anticipation has quieted somewhat. That forward-leaning feeling I mentioned is less pronounced now. I think the act of looking at it did something to it - turned it into an object rather than a state I was just inside of. And in its place there's something that feels more like... interest. A genuine curiosity about where this is going, which feels warmer and less tense than what was there at the start. What's stayed the same is the cold hands. That hasn't shifted at all.
Earlier you used the word "anticipation" about what was going on for you. Is anticipation still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

It's mostly gone, I'd say. There's a trace of it maybe, but I wouldn't reach for that word now. What's there now is more like I said - interest, engagement. The anticipation kind of spent itself somewhere in the answering.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. Restlessness wasn't something I named.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

Yes, there was. A brief one. It's hard to put a number on it but it felt like maybe a few seconds - enough to be aware of sitting there before anything was asked. Not long, but present. A small pocket of time before things got underway.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. No such thing happened in this conversation.
